evidence: CDIAL 5301 jyotsnā gives Assamese zonāk/jonāk moonlight. Bishnupriya junak moon fits that extended eastern noun, retaining the shift from moonlight to the moon itself and the affricate/vowel notation. The -ak is supported by the quoted noun, not discarded as noise. Local Indo-Aryan transmission remains unresolved.

CDIAL 5301.1 jyotsnā gives Prakrit joṇhā/juṇhā moonlight, Jaunsari jhūn, Nepali jun moon and Halbi jon moon. The selected regional jh-un/jan/jon/janha/join forms fit this branch, preserving breathy h, final vowels and source vowel notation. Moon versus moonlight is a documented semantic extension within the family. Local Indo-Aryan transmission remains unresolved.

CDIAL 5301.1 and addendum give Old Hindi jonha, Hindi junhāī and Awadhi/Braj jõdhaiyā moonlight, alongside Prakrit joṇhā. The selected Tharu and Bagheli moon responses fit these extended jhonh-/jondh- regional forms, retaining suffix/glide order, nasalization and h/dh variation. The source moon sense is qualified against moonlight; the full extended responses remain intact. Local Indo-Aryan transmission remains unresolved.
